Thanks Hannah — looping in technical details below and a proposed owner/timeline.

Summary for deck (1 page):
- What the tile shows: per-route P50/P95 latency, per-route token spend (30d window), sample rate, sample coverage %, and links to trace playback & tenant billing page.
- Guarantee model: we can offer a best-effort "priority sampling" lane that increases sampling rate for tagged routes and surfaces preserved KV cache windows for a configurable incident window (1–4 hours).
- Hard limits: we cannot guarantee 100% full-fidelity on extremely bursty tails unless the customer buys reserved Dedicated burst capacity. There is an incremental cost estimate for different protection levels (priority sampling only; sampling+bump of reserved capacity; full bypass if on Dedicated).

Technical notes (for appendix) — Jasmine, please confirm these numbers are accurate before I finalize:
- Default sample rate: adaptive by token path, today ~1.2% of requests for high-volume tenants; priority lane target: 15–25% (depending on quota headroom).
- Expected cost delta (Acme-scale baseline): priority lane ~+8–18% token spend; priority + 2h cache pinning ~+12–30%; Dedicated bypass estimate: depends on committed GPU hours, see appendix.
- Implementation work: telemetry tag (tenant.route.sla_priority) + CLI/console flag to flip priority for a tenant; dashboard tile that pulls from consolidated metrics pipeline (Prometheus + per-tenant rollups).

Owner/timeline proposal:
- Marcus: produce 1-pager + cost appendix (today -> EOD)
- Jasmine: confirm numbers and attach sampling mock (by 3pm PDT)
- Irene: finalize wording on guaranteed vs recommended language, and sign off on public-facing SLA phrasing (by 5pm PDT)

I'll draft the PDF and send over when Jasmine confirms the sampling figures.

— Marcus
Director, Product — Console & Observability
Redwood Inference

Marcus — numbers below and a short implementation note. Quoted original for context: 

> Default sample rate: adaptive by token path, today ~1.2% of requests for high-volume tenants; priority lane target: 15–25% (depending on quota headroom).

Confirmed. On our staging telemetry for a tenant with ~2B tokens/month we see:
- Baseline capture rate: 1.1–1.4% (adaptive).
- Priority lane (configurable): 15% default, configurable up to 30% for the incident window.
- Coverage: priority lane increases route-level event coverage from ~24% to ~92% for common call paths (depends on path diversity).

Cost estimates validated against current token-pipeline:
- Priority 15%: +9% spend (tokenization + storage + per-token infra).
- Priority 25%: +15% spend.
- Cache pinning (2h): +6% incremental on top of priority lane (due to extra KV hotness and replay work).

Implementation notes:
- Small console change: tenant settings -> toggle "Incident priority sampling" with a duration field. Backend work: ~3 engineer-weeks (1 infra, 1 telemetry, 1 console).
- Short-term workaround if procurement needs immediate language: we can promise a "priority sampling" SLA (X% coverage target) with a caveat: "when not in Dedicated with committed burst capacity, we may throttle priority lanes during global capacity exhaustion". That caveat must be in the procurement doc.

I'll attach the sampling mock (dashboard_mock_sampling.png) used in the deck and a short appendix snippet you can paste into the PDF.

— Jasmine
Senior SRE, Observability
Redwood Inference
